fullPassage: In Vallauris, a small town in the South of France, a black limousine was parked outside a barbershop. From inside the car, Pablo Picasso impatiently yelled out. “Please, Arias, hurry up. We’ll be late for dinner.” A curious crowd gathered around the car, wondering who had the nerve to make the legendary artist wait. A few moments later, Eugenio Arias, a man with a cheerful smile, emerged from his modest shop. “Let’s go,” he said as he climbed into the limousine. Despite the fact that Picasso was twenty-eight years older than Arias, the two had been close friends for twenty years. Let’s go back to that summer afternoon when their friendship across generations began. In 1947, Picasso left the crowded city of Paris and moved to the quiet rural town of Vallauris. As a foreigner, he often desperately longed for familiar faces from his home country, Spain. One day, a friend told him about a local barber from Spain named Arias. But for Picasso, it was not easy to visit the barbershop because he had a belief that anyone who possessed his hair or nails would have control over him. Too superstitious to let other people cut his hair, he normally chose to cut his own hair. Eventually, Picasso gathered his courage and entered Arias’s barbershop because he was so eager to meet his fellow countryman. Arias recognized the famous artist right away, but he treated Picasso like an ordinary customer. Leading him to a chair, Arias warmly welcomed Picasso in Spanish. Despite the fact that their conversation was brief that day, Picasso was deeply impressed by Arias’s direct and simple manner of speech. He sensed that Arias was a trustworthy individual with a great sense of humor who put people at ease. Picasso’s visits to Arias’s barbershop became somewhat routine after that. Whenever he visited, the other customers let him be served first. This situation made Picasso feel uncomfortable because it caused other people to wait longer. Sensing his discomfort, Arias asked if Picasso would prefer to get haircuts and shaves at home. Picasso happily accepted the offer. Arias went to Picasso’s house to cut his hair from then on, but he never charged Picasso for his services. In return, Picasso gave him sketches, paintings, and ceramics as a gesture of friendship. As their friendship grew stronger, Arias started to drop by Picasso’s house, not to shave or cut his hair, but to hang out. Picasso once said to Arias, “You are always welcome to come to my house. When you’re here, I feel like I’m back in Spain.” Picasso also paid frequent visits to Arias’s home, where he enjoyed Spanish dishes prepared by Arias’s mother. When they dined together, they would sit and talk for hours. Picasso once asked Arias, “What do you think about your own work as a barber?” Arias answered, “Well, when I finish a haircut for a customer, I always notice my mistakes.” Upon hearing Arias’s response, Picasso suddenly hugged him and said, “You’re an artist. I always see some mistakes whenever I finish my paintings.” One day, Picasso was busy painting War and Peace, one of his largest projects, when Arias paid him a visit. Picasso had been working hard staying up at night for days. Seeing this, Arias assisted Picasso with his work, from moving a ladder around for Picasso to painting some characters. So Picasso made a joke, “Now I have to sign this painting Picasso and Arias.” As time passed, Picasso’s health declined with age. One day, Picasso asked Arias, “What are you going to do with all the paintings and sketches I gave you?” Arias responded that he would build a museum in Spain to display the works. Picasso was moved to hear that and swore to help Arias. But unfortunately, he did not live to see the museum completed, passing away in 1973. Arias was in grief and despair but found comfort in knowing that his best friend would live on through his art. A few years later, Arias returned to Spain and exhibited Picasso’s works. This small exhibit attracted visitors from all over the world. A foreign merchant approached Arias one day and attempted to persuade him to sell all of Picasso’s works. But he refused to bargain, saying, “Even if you bring all the money in your country, I will not sell any of his works to you. His works are symbols of the friendship between Picasso and me.” The Museo Picasso - Colección Eugenio Arias (The Picasso Museum - Eugenio Arias Collection) was finally completed. This was possible because Arias donated approximately sixty pieces of Picasso’s works to Arias’s hometown of Buitrago del Lozoya. They comprised a collection of paintings, posters, ceramics, and other works. Each of them is distinct from Picasso’s other works because Picasso carved each one with the inscription Para mi amigo, Arias (For my friend, Arias). When visitors enter this museum, they quickly discover that it is more than just a tribute to honor Picasso’s artistic legacy; it is also a monument to the artist and barber’s lifelong friendship. The Museo Picasso - Colección Eugenio

✅ ① 'he did not live to see the museum completed, passing away in 1973'에서 미술관 완공을 보지 못하고 1973년에 떠났다고 했으므로 일치한다

✅ ② 'found comfort in knowing that his best friend would live on through his art'에서 친구가 예술로 살아남으리라는 데서 위안을 얻었다고 했으므로 일치한다

❌ ③ 본문은 'he refused to bargain ~ I will not sell any of his works'라 하여 아리아스가 흥정을 '거부하고' 팔지 않겠다고 했다. 따라서 '모두 팔아 큰돈을 벌었다'는 정반대이므로 일치하지 않는다 ← 정답

✅ ④ 'Arias donated approximately sixty pieces of Picasso's works to Arias's hometown'에서 약 예순 점을 고향에 기증했다고 했으므로 일치한다
det.tip: refused to bargain / will not sell ↔ '모두 팔아 큰돈을 벌었다'는 정반대

questions.passage: In Vallauris, a small town in the South of France, a black limousine was parked outside a barbershop.  From inside the car, Pablo Picasso impatiently yelled out.  “Please, Arias, hurry up.  We’ll be late for dinner. ” A curious crowd gathered around the car, wondering who had the nerve to make the legendary artist wait.  A few moments later, Eugenio Arias, a man with a cheerful smile, emerged from his modest shop.  “Let’s go,” he said as he climbed into the limousine.  Despite the fact that Picasso was twenty-eight years older than Arias, the two had been close friends for twenty years.  Let’s go back to that summer afternoon when their friendship across generations began.  In 1947, Picasso left the crowded city of Paris and moved to the quiet rural town of Vallauris.  As a foreigner, he often desperately longed for familiar faces from his home country, Spain.  One day, a friend told him about a local barber from Spain named Arias.  But for Picasso, it was not easy to visit the barbershop because he had a belief that anyone who possessed his hair or nails would have control over him.  Too superstitious to let other people cut his hair, he normally chose to cut his own hair.  Eventually, Picasso gathered his courage and entered Arias’s barbershop because he was so eager to meet his fellow countryman.  Arias recognized the famous artist right away, but he treated Picasso like an ordinary customer.  Leading him to a chair, Arias warmly welcomed Picasso in Spanish.  Despite the fact that their conversation was brief that day, Picasso was deeply impressed by Arias’s direct and simple manner of speech.  He sensed that Arias was a trustworthy individual with a great sense of humor who put people at ease.  Picasso’s visits to Arias’s barbershop became somewhat routine after that.  Whenever he visited, the other customers let him be served first.  This situation made Picasso feel uncomfortable because it caused other people to wait longer.  Sensing his discomfort, Arias asked if Picasso would prefer to get haircuts and shaves at home.  Picasso happily accepted the offer.  Arias went to Picasso’s house to cut his hair from then on, but he never charged Picasso for his services.  In return, Picasso gave him sketches, paintings, and ceramics as a gesture of friendship.  As their friendship grew stronger, Arias started to drop by Picasso’s house, not to shave or cut his hair, but to hang out.  Picasso once said to Arias, “You are always welcome to come to my house.  When you’re here, I feel like I’m back in Spain. ” Picasso also paid frequent visits to Arias’s home, where he enjoyed Spanish dishes prepared by Arias’s mother.  When they dined together, they would sit and talk for hours.  Picasso once asked Arias, “What do you think about your own work as a barber? ” Arias answered, “Well, when I finish a haircut for a customer, I always notice my mistakes. ” Upon hearing Arias’s response, Picasso suddenly hugged him and said, “You’re an artist.  I always see some mistakes whenever I finish my paintings. ” One day, Picasso was busy painting War and Peace, one of his largest projects, when Arias paid him a visit.  Picasso had been working hard staying up at night for days.  Seeing this, Arias assisted Picasso with his work, from moving a ladder around for Picasso to painting some characters.  So Picasso made a joke, “Now I have to sign this painting Picasso and Arias. ” As time passed, Picasso’s health declined with age.  One day, Picasso asked Arias, “What are you going to do with all the paintings and sketches I gave you? ” Arias responded that he would build a museum in Spain to display the works.  Picasso was moved to hear that and swore to help Arias.  But unfortunately, he did not live to see the museum completed, passing away in 1973.  Arias was in grief and despair but found comfort in knowing that his best friend would live on through his art.  A few years later, Arias returned to Spain and exhibited Picasso’s works.  This small exhibit attracted visitors from all over the world.  A foreign merchant approached Arias one day and attempted to persuade him to sell all of Picasso’s works.  But he refused to bargain, saying, “Even if you bring all the money in your country, I will not sell any of his works to you.  His works are symbols of the friendship between Picasso and me. ” The Museo Picasso - Colección Eugenio Arias (The Picasso Museum - Eugenio Arias Collection) was finally completed.  This was possible because Arias donated approximately sixty pieces of Picasso’s works to Arias’s hometown of Buitrago del Lozoya.  They comprised a collection of paintings, posters, ceramics, and other works.  Each of them is distinct from Picasso’s other works because Picasso carved each one with the inscription Para mi amigo, Arias (For my friend, Arias).

❌ ③ 이민자의 문화적 어려움: 지엽적 소재로 글 전체를 대표하지 못한다

✅ ④ 나이·지위를 뛰어넘은 우정: 글 전체가 스물여덟 살 차이의 세계적 화가와 이발사가 20년간 나눈 우정과, 그 우정을 기린 미술관 이야기를 다루므로 주제로 알맞다 ← 정답
det.tip: 화가와 이발사의 세대·신분을 초월한 평생의 우정이 전체 주제

det.korean: ① A Priceless Friendship Beyond Age and Status (나이와 지위를 초월한 값을 매길 수 없는 우정)
det.analysis:
✅ ① A Priceless Friendship Beyond Age and Status(나이와 지위를 초월한, 값을 매길 수 없는 우정): 스물여덟 살 차이의 화가와 이발사가 나눈, 돈으로 살 수 없는 우정이라는 글 전체를 아우르므로 제목으로 알맞다 ← 정답

❌ ② The Secret Techniques of a Master Barber(名이발사의 비밀 기술): 이발 기술을 다룬 글이 아니므로 부적절하다

❌ ③ How Picasso Conquered the European Art World(피카소가 유럽 미술계를 정복한 방법): 피카소의 성공기가 아니라 우정에 관한 글이라 부적절하다

❌ ④ The Rise and Fall of the Modern Art Market(현대 미술 시장의 흥망성쇠): 미술 시장의 경제 이야기가 아니므로 부적절하다

det.korean: ④ 스페인 출신으로 이발소를 운영하는 남자 (= 아리아스)
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장 'he never charged Picasso for his services'에서 바로 앞에 있는 이름은 Picasso지만, 함정에 주의해야 한다. 요금을 청구하는 쪽은 서비스를 제공하는 이발사이므로, 'his services(그의 서비스)'는 피카소의 집에 찾아가 머리를 잘라 준 이발사 아리아스의 서비스를 가리킨다.

❌ ① 유명한 화가: 피카소는 서비스를 받는 손님이지 제공하는 쪽이 아니므로 틀리다

❌ ② 호기심 많은 군중: 이발 서비스와 무관하다

❌ ③ 음식을 만든 노부인: 아리아스의 어머니로, 이발 서비스와 무관하다

✅ ④ 이발소를 운영하는 남자: 피카소의 머리를 잘라 주고도 요금을 받지 않은 이발사 아리아스를 가리키므로 알맞다 ← 정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 across generations(세대를 뛰어넘어)가 적절
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에서 피카소가 아리아스보다 '스물여덟 살 더 많았다(twenty-eight years older)'고 했으므로, 두 사람의 우정은 큰 나이 차, 즉 세대 차이를 뛰어넘은 것임을 알 수 있다.

✅ ① across generations(세대를 뛰어넘어): 스물여덟 살 차이를 넘어선 우정이라는 흐름에 딱 맞는다 ← 정답

❌ ② within a single family(한 가족 안에서): 두 사람은 가족이 아니므로 부적절하다

❌ ③ between old business rivals(오랜 사업 경쟁자 사이의): 우정에 관한 글이므로 경쟁자는 어울리지 않는다

❌ ④ only for financial profit(오로지 금전적 이익을 위한): 돈이 아닌 진심 어린 우정이므로 정반대다
det.tip: 스물여덟 살 나이 차 → 세대를 뛰어넘은(across generations) 우정

questions.passage: Sensing his discomfort, Arias asked if Picasso would prefer to get haircuts and shaves at home.  Picasso happily accepted the offer.  Arias went to Picasso’s house to cut his hair from then on, but __________.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 [조건]에 맞게 빈칸을 (영어로) 쓰시오.

그런데 그는 자신의 서비스에 대해 피카소에게 결코 요금을 청구하지 않았다.

[조건] (1) Picasso, charged, for, he, his, never, services 를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: he never charged Picasso for his services (7단어)
det.analysis: '그는 ~에 대해 결코 요금을 청구하지 않았다'가 핵심이다. 주어 he로 시작하고, '결코 ~않다'라는 부정 부사 never를 동사 앞에 놓아 'he never charged(그는 결코 청구하지 않았다)'를 만든다. 그다음 '누구에게'에 해당하는 목적어 Picasso를 쓰고, '~에 대해'를 뜻하는 전치사 for로 이어 'for his services(그의 서비스에 대해)'를 붙인다. 순서는 he → never → charged → Picasso → for → his → services이다.
det.tip: 부정 부사 never는 일반동사 charged 앞: he never charged ~

questions.wa: he never charged Picasso for his services
accept: he never charged Picasso for his services

A foreign merchant approached Arias one day and attempted ②<u>to persuade</u> him to sell all of Picasso’s works.  But he refused to bargain, ③<u>said</u>, “Even if you bring all the money in your country, I will not sell any of his works to you.  His ④<u>works are symbols</u> of the friendship between Picasso and me.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것을 하나 찾아 바르게 고쳐 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: ③ said → saying (동시동작을 나타내는 분사구문)
det.analysis:
✅ ① exhibited: 'Arias returned to Spain and exhibited Picasso's works(스페인으로 돌아가 피카소의 작품을 전시했다)'에서 and로 앞의 returned와 나란히 이어지는 과거시제 동사로 알맞다

✅ ② to persuade: 'attempted to persuade him to sell(그에게 팔라고 설득하려 했다)'에서 'attempt to+동사원형(~하려고 시도하다)' 구문의 to부정사로 알맞다

❌ ③ said → saying: 'But he refused to bargain, said, ...'가 문제다. 앞에 refused라는 동사가 이미 있는데 접속사 없이 said를 또 쓸 수 없다. '~라고 말하면서'라는 동시동작을 나타내는 분사구문이 되어야 하므로 현재분사 saying으로 고쳐야 한다 ← 정답

✅ ④ works are symbols: 'His works are symbols of the friendship(그의 작품들은 우정의 상징이다)'에서 주어 works가 복수이므로 복수 동사 are로 수를 맞춘 것은 알맞다
det.tip: 동사 두 개(refused ~ said)를 접속사 없이 나열 불가 → 분사구문 saying(말하면서)

나는 그의 작품 중 어느 것도 팔지 않겠다.

[조건] (1) I, any, his, not, of, sell, will, works 를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: I will not sell any of his works (8단어)
det.analysis: '나는 ~하지 않겠다'라는 미래의 강한 거절은 조동사 will의 부정 'will not'으로 나타낸다. 그래서 주어 I 다음에 will → not → 동사원형 sell 순으로 놓는다. '그의 작품 중 어느 것도'는 부정문에서 '어느 것도'를 뜻하는 any를 써서 'any of his works(그의 작품 중 어느 것)'로 표현한다. 순서는 I → will → not → sell → any → of → his → works이다.
det.tip: 부정문의 '어느 것도' = any of ~ / 강한 거절 = will not

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 빈칸을 (영어로) 쓰시오. (12단어)

그것은 또한 예술가와 이발사의 평생에 걸친 우정을 기리는 기념물이기도 하다.

[단어] a, also, and, artist, barber's, friendship, is, it, lifelong, monument, the, to

det.korean: it is also a monument to the artist and barber’s lifelong friendship (12단어)
det.analysis: '그것은 또한 ~이기도 하다'는 'it is also ~'로 시작한다. be동사 is 뒤에 부사 also를 놓고, 보어인 명사구 'a monument(기념물)'를 이어 쓴다. '~을 기리는/~에 대한'은 전치사 to로 연결해 'to the artist and barber's ~'로 이어 준다. 마지막으로 '평생에 걸친 우정'은 형용사 lifelong이 명사 friendship을 꾸며 'lifelong friendship'이 된다. 순서는 it → is → also → a → monument → to → the → artist → and → barber's → lifelong → friendship이다.
det.tip: it is also + a monument to + (the artist and barber's) lifelong friendship

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 [조건]에 맞게 빈칸을 (영어로) 쓰시오.

그는 그 미술관이 완성되는 것을 보지 못했다.

[조건] (1) completed, did, he, live, museum, not, see, the, to 를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: he did not live to see the museum completed (9단어)
det.analysis: '그는 ~하지 못했다'라는 과거의 부정은 'did not + 동사원형'으로 나타내므로 'he did not live(그는 살지 못했다)'로 시작한다. '~하는 것을 볼 만큼 (오래) 살지 못했다'는 뜻을 살려 목적을 나타내는 to see(보기 위해/보도록)를 이어 쓴다. 마지막으로 '그 미술관이 완성되는 것'은 지각동사 see의 목적어 the museum이 '완성되는' 대상이므로 수동을 뜻하는 과거분사 completed를 목적격보어로 놓아 'see the museum completed'로 만든다. 순서는 he → did → not → live → to → see → the → museum → completed이다.
det.tip: did not live to see + 목적어(the museum) + 과거분사(completed)

accept: he did not live to see the museum completed
